title: Shortness of Breath
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, fatigue, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on CXR. May have erythema nodosum (painful red nodules on shins), uveitis, parotid enlargement, lupus pernio (purplish facial plaques). Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disease of unknown etiology — more common in African Americans. Non-caseating granulomas are the pathologic hallmark. CXR staging: I (BHL only), II (BHL + parenchymal infiltrates), III (parenchymal only), IV (fibrosis). Labs: elevated ACE level (supports but not diagnostic), hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria (increased 1,25-vitamin D from activated macrophages in granulomas). Diagnosis: biopsy showing non-caseating granulomas + exclusion of other causes (TB, fungal, berylliosis). PFTs: restrictive pattern. Treatment: many resolve spontaneously (stage I). If symptomatic or progressive → corticosteroids (prednisone 0.5 mg/kg/day). Methotrexate or azathioprine for steroid-sparing. Anti-TNF for refractory. Monitor for TB reactivation before immunosuppression.
chief_complaint: Progressive dyspnea, dry cough, bilateral hilar adenopathy

stacks.label: Prednisone (if symptomatic)
stacks.finding: First-line. Taper to lowest effective dose.
